skill.name: Privy
skill.description: Guidance for building Privy authentication, embedded wallet, policy, transaction, and webhook integrations across client and server applications.
skill.summary: Plan and review Privy wallet, authentication, policy, transaction, and webhook integrations.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command and network alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline API names, official Privy URLs, and documentation links. The cryptocurrency wallet alert is confirmed because the skill guides server-side blockchain transaction execution, which can move assets if misused. No prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or deceptive marketplace claims were found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings that production transactions need testnet validation, policy review, signer authorization, and human approval for asset movement.
Show secrets loaded from environment variables and state that App Secret and webhook secrets must never appear in client bundles.
Label REST and curl examples as manual integration references and avoid wording that suggests automatic execution by an AI agent.

- **Webhook verification required:** Always verify webhook signatures before trusting the payload. U

- **Missing app client ID:** If deploying across multiple domains, configure app clients in the Dash

content.user_title: Build Privy Wallet and Auth Integrations
content.value_statement: Wallet and authentication integrations are difficult to design safely across clients, servers, and chains. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise Privy guidance for setup, wallet creation, policies, transactions, and webhooks.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes Privy core concepts, including users, embedded wallets, owners, signers, policies, and intents.
Shows React, Node.js, and REST entry points for starting a Privy integration.
Compares embedded wallets, external wallets, client-side wallets, server-side wallets, and Privy Auth.
Outlines a workflow for app setup, user authentication, wallet creation, policies, transactions, and webhooks.
Lists operational checks for secrets, chain IDs, units, signatures, idempotency, and rate limits.
limitations: It is a guidance skill, not a replacement for Privy documentation or legal review.
It does not verify live Privy API behavior, pricing, service limits, or dashboard settings.
It does not generate a complete production security model for custody, approvals, or compliance.
It cannot execute transactions or validate wallet balances by itself.

use_cases.title: Design user onboarding
use_cases.description: Choose login methods, embedded wallet behavior, and client setup for a new application using Privy.

use_cases.title: Plan server wallet operations
use_cases.description: Map wallet creation, signer permissions, transaction submission, policy checks, and webhook processing before backend implementation.

use_cases.title: Review launch readiness
use_cases.description: Check secrets, policies, chain identifiers, numeric units, webhook verification, idempotency, and rate-limit handling before release.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a wallet model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new app
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which Privy wallet model fits my consumer app. Compare embedded wallets and external wallets for users who sign their own transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Create an auth checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an implementation checklist for adding Privy Auth to a React app. Include readiness checks, login methods, and secure credential handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review transaction flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned server-side wallet flow for Privy. Identify policy, approval, idempotency, webhook, and unit-conversion risks before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Design treasury controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Privy integration plan for a multi-chain treasury app. Cover ownership, signer roles, policy constraints, event monitoring, and rollback planning.

output_examples.input: Plan Privy setup for a React app with email login and embedded wallets.
output: Use the Privy provider component at the application root.
Enable email login and embedded wallet creation in the dashboard.
Wait for the ready state before reading user or wallet data.

output_examples.input: Review a server-side wallet transaction flow.
output: Confirm wallet ownership and signer permissions before submitting transactions.
Test policy decisions with expected recipients, amounts, and chain identifiers.
Use idempotency keys and monitor webhook events after submission.

output_examples.input: Prepare a launch checklist for Privy webhooks.
output: Register the webhook endpoint in the dashboard.
Verify every webhook signature before trusting payload data.
Add retries, logging controls, and incident alerts for failed processing.

best_practices: Store App Secret and webhook secrets outside source code and client bundles.
Use policies, approvals, and idempotency keys for transaction paths that move assets.
Verify webhook signatures and test chain IDs, units, and rate-limit handling before launch.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding secrets in examples, commits, or browser-executed code.
Sending transactions before testing policy decisions, units, and approval requirements.
Trusting webhook payloads without signature verification.

faq.question: Can this skill create wallets for me?
faq.answer: No. It explains Privy concepts and integration steps. You must implement and authorize wallet creation in your application.

faq.question: Does it support Ethereum and Solana?
faq.answer: Yes. The source covers Ethereum and Solana examples, and mentions several other supported chains.

faq.question: Can it replace Privy documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it for quick guidance, then verify current API details in official Privy documentation.

faq.question: Is it safe for production wallet custody decisions?
faq.answer: Use it as planning help only. Review custody, compliance, approvals, and incident response with qualified teams.

faq.question: Does it expose secrets?
faq.answer: The skill contains placeholder credentials and advises secure storage. Do not paste real secrets into prompts or client code.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
